title: Sentinel prober and confidence-delta fallback orchestrator for optimistic decode
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Implement a lightweight "sentinel" prober and an acceptance-scoring fallback orchestrator designed to enable optimistic (speculative) decoding while bounding correctness regressions and cost. The sentinel prober issues a short, cost-limited prefill+decode probe to alternate candidate models (or faster kernel variants) to get early acceptance signals. The orchestrator computes a confidence-delta score comparing the primary route and candidate route outputs and decides whether to continue on the optimistic path or to fall back to the safe route. This ticket covers design, runtime changes in the scheduler, kernel-aware probe placement, telemetry, experiments, and rollout/revert criteria.
acceptance_criteria: Runtime exposes a prober API that can send a bounded prefill+N-token probe to a candidate model variant without blocking the main request path
Acceptance scoring function implemented in router: accepts when confidence-delta <= threshold and probe latency < probe_timeout
Fallback orchestrator can cancel optimistic decode and transparently switch to safe route with no client-visible corruption (streaming resume or full redecode path implemented)
End-to-end telemetry emitted: probe latency, probe token cross-entropy, confidence-delta histogram, fallback reasons, and cost delta per request
Performance targets met in experiments: median latency reduction vs. safe-only baseline >= 10% for short responses (<=64 tokens) with false-accept rate <= 1% on held-out prompt set
Feature behind runtime flag + rollout controls in Console with canary buckets and percentage rollout
telemetry_goals: Emit probe.trace_id and link to request.trace_id for correlation
rollout_plan: Stage 0: Unit tests + integration tests in CI. Runtime flag default=off
Stage 1: Internal canary: enable for 1% of requests in staging with synthetic load and run heavy instrumentation
Stage 2: 5% experiment in production on low-SLA customer bucket (no billing impact) for 48h
Stage 3: 25% ramp with automated monitoring checks; if false-accept rate > 1.5% or p99 latency regressions > 5% -> pause
Stage 4: Gradual to 100% with console controls and per-customer opt-out for Dedicated/Private
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Probe adds tail load and increases overall cost. Mitigation: probe budget per-second per-GPU, rate-limit probes and prefer cheaper quantized candidate variants for probing

Risk: False accept leads to subtle semantic drift visible to users. Mitigation: conservative initial thresholds, holdout evaluation on production traffic, and automatic rollback on quality regression alerts
Risk: Probe latency interfering with main-path SLOs. Mitigation: probe on separate scheduler pool with kernel-hotspot awareness and preemption disabled for main-path tokens
Risk: Complexity in streaming resume when fallback occurs mid-stream. Mitigation: implement atomic stream switch with idempotent start offset and client-visible marker to request resync if needed
todo: Finalize acceptance scoring formula (proposed: confidence_delta = CE_primary_probe - CE_candidate_probe; accept if <= 0.15) and tune on evaluation corpora

Add kernel-signature tagging for candidate models so router can pick kernel-friendly probe targets
